question: For a set of observations, the mean is 8 and standard deviation is 3. then the coefficient of dispersion is equal to:
solution:
The correct answer is 37.5.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Coefficient of Dispersion Calculation:**

 
 
• The coefficient of dispersion is calculated using the formula: (Standard Deviation / Mean) * 100.
 
• In this case, it is (3 / 8) * 100 = 37.5.
 
• This value indicates the relative variability of the data set in percentage terms.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incorrect Options:**

 
 
• **Option 2 (20.3):** This value is incorrect as it does not match the calculation (3/8) * 100.
 
• **Option 3 (27.2):** This value is also incorrect and does not align with the formula for the coefficient of dispersion.
 
• **Option 4 (32.7):** This option is incorrect as well, as it does not correspond to the correct computation of the coefficient of dispersion.
